question: Should maintainers authorize the exact-head dependency graph change for the new `@openclaw/workboard` UI dependency, or require this branch to remove/rework that graph change before merge?
rationale: The code direction is plausible, but repository policy blocks dependency graph changes until admin/secops authorizes the exact head, and the new package export is an API/compatibility boundary that automation should not approve by inference.

options.title: Authorize after security review
options.body: Review the workspace dependency, package export, and lockfile importer diff, then have an admin or secops member approve the exact head if this is the intended seam.

options.title: Remove the dependency graph change
options.body: Ask the author to rework the branch so Control UI does not add a new workspace dependency or lockfile entry before the package seam is accepted.

options.title: Pause for a different seam
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer merge while maintainers choose a different owner boundary for Workboard UI contracts.

recommendation.title: Authorize after security review
recommendation.body: Review the workspace dependency, package export, and lockfile importer diff, then have an admin or secops member approve the exact head if this is the intended seam.

likelyOwner.reason: RomneyDa owns this PR and the linked staged contract-canonicalization issue, so they are the best visible owner for explaining whether the dependency/package seam is intentional.
